title: Power Apps: build model-driven apps with Copilot Cowork
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing statements and documented governance controls are supported. It appropriately separates the planned Cowork skill from the documented code-tools skill and leaves the Cowork-specific environment, connection and default state unconfirmed.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance guidance; controls[0].note
claims.claim: A spending policy that includes the user and selects Cowork grants Cowork access.
claims.quote: A user has access to Cowork when a policy's scope includes them (directly through All users, or through a security group) and that policy selects Cowork under Select agents and services.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: A low credit limit does not block Cowork access.
claims.quote: Any user in the scope of a spending policy that selects Cowork can use Cowork, regardless of how small the credit limit is. A policy with a limit of one credit still grants access.

claims.claim: Removing a user from every spending policy selecting Cowork removes their access.
claims.quote: To remove access for a user, remove them from every spending policy that includes Cowork.

claims.claim: Configuration on the Cowork entry under Agents > All Agents has no effect on access.
claims.quote: The Cowork agent entry is still visible under Agents > All Agents, but any configuration on it has no effect on who can use Cowork.

claims.claim: Asynchronous credit enforcement can allow users to start tasks after reaching a limit.
claims.quote: Credit limits are a spending safeguard, not a real-time access gate. Credit consumption and limit enforcement are evaluated asynchronously, so a user might be able to start one or more tasks after their limit is reached before enforcement takes effect.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 spending-policy path through Identity, Specific groups and Cowork reaches Set limits and alerts.
claims.quote: Copilot > Cost Management ... Configuration ... + Add spending policy ... choose Identity as the scope ... Specific groups ... Select agents and services ... Set limits and alerts

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies creates a policy with serviceSettings, periodLimit and perUserLimit, including serviceId cowork with state enabled.
Group-scoped policies are created disabled and their audience must be linked before the service enables them.
claims.quote: For a group-scoped policy, follow the safe-create sequence: create the policy disabled, link its audience with Add assigned group, and let the service enable it once its requirements are satisfied.

claims.claim: A Cowork plugin can be blocked in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Agents > Tools > plugin > Users > Block.
claims.quote:
select Agents > Tools.
Find the plugin you want to manage and go to the Users tab.
Select Block: No users in your tenant can access the plugin.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package.
claims.quote:
Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All
Delegated (personal Microsoft account) | Not supported.
Application | Not available.

claims.claim: The Power Platform admin center path Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > user > Manage security roles reaches direct user role management.
claims.quote: select Manage ... select Environments, and then select an environment ... Select Settings ... Select Users + permissions, and then select Users ... select a user, and then select Manage security roles.

claims.claim: pac admin assign-user --environment <environment-id> --user <upn> --role "<role-name>" assigns the specified security role to the user in the target environment.
claims.quote:
Assign a user to a target Dataverse environment with specified security role.
--role: Name or ID of security role to be applied to user
--user: Object ID or user principal name (UPN)
--environment: ID or URL of the environment to assign a user to.

claims.claim: System Administrator is the default role with the privileges to assign security roles.
claims.quote: By default, the System Administrator security role has all the required privileges to assign security roles to any user, including assigning the System Administrator security role.
